sections.html:
• Scientific name: Liobagrus mediadiposalis Mori, 1936
  • Common names: South Torrent Catfish, Jagasari (Korean)
  • Type locality: Rakuto River at Bun-kei, Chosen, Korea.
  • Pronunciation: lie oh BAG russ
  • Size: 133 mm or 5.2 in SL.
  • IUCN Red List category: Least Concern. Last assessed 2023.

• Dorsal spines: 1; dorsal soft rays: 6; anal spines: 0; anal soft rays: 14-17

Etymology: -alis, adjectival suffix; media-, middle, presumably referring to the high and long adipose fin centered on the back between the dorsal and caudal fins.
Southern Asia: China, Japan and Korea waters.

Asia: Rivers of Natong, Kokson, Yongsan, Kim and Tchongchin, Korea. Type locality: River Rakuto at Bun-kei, Chosen, Korea.

This species is observed in central and southern parts of the Korean Peninsula, where it is endemic.

Endemic to Korea and inhabits the rocky or stony bottoms of rocky streams. The streams are well oxygenated but during the summer dry season, they become hypoxic. L. mediadiposalis may be able to absorb oxygen through the skin during this period.

• pH: 6.5 - 7.5
  • Temperature: 17.0-25.0°C (62.6-77°F)

These fish reside in the temperate zone and undergo a wide range of temperatures throughout the year. They may tolerate higher and lower temperatures for a short period of time. Torrent-like conditions are not necessary, though the water should have some flow. The filter outflow is generally adequate.
Etymology: From the Greek, leios, meaning smooth, and bagrus, a name usually used for catfishes; in reference to the smooth head. Named after the genus Amblyceps, which refers to its blunt head.

IUCN Red List: Despite evidence to suggest that some habitats along the Geum River have been destroyed, no major threats to the species have been identified so far and there are no reports of population declines. This species is assessed as Least Concern, but it is recommended that threats and population trends be investigated (IUCN 2023).
Dobutsugaku Zasshi = Zoological Magazine Tokyo v. 48 (nos 8-10), pp 673, Pl. 24 (fig. 3).
